problem: Assign 4 engineers (Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave) to 4 distinct roles (backend, frontend, devops, qa). Each engineer gets exactly one role and each role goes to exactly one engineer. Three hard eligibility constraints restrict the assignment.

constraints.description: Bob must be assigned backend or frontend
Each engineer gets exactly one distinct role (bijective assignment)

steps: c1 removes devops from alice → alice: {backend, frontend, qa}
c2 removes devops and qa from bob → bob: {backend, frontend}
c3 removes qa from carol → carol: {backend, frontend, devops}
MRV: pick bob (size 2). Try bob = backend.
c4 (alldiff): remove backend from alice, carol, dave → alice: {frontend, qa}, carol: {frontend, devops}, dave: {frontend, devops, qa}
MRV: pick alice (size 2). Try alice = frontend.
c4 (alldiff): remove frontend from carol, dave → carol: {devops} (size 1, forced), dave: {devops, qa}
c4 (alldiff): remove devops from dave → dave: {qa} (size 1, forced).
dave = qa. All domains are singletons — solution complete.

analysis: Arc consistency propagation, guided by the Minimum Remaining Values (MRV) heuristic, solved this CSP entirely without backtracking. Fixing bob=backend via MRV cascaded through alldiff to shrink all other domains; alice's selection of frontend then forced carol→devops and dave→qa by unit propagation. Verification: alice=frontend satisfies c1 (≠devops) ✓; bob=backend satisfies c2 (∈{backend,frontend}) ✓; carol=devops satisfies c3 (≠qa) ✓; all four values are distinct, satisfying c4 ✓. Note: this is a feasibility result only — the assignment is not claimed to be 'optimal'. If preferences existed (e.g., prefer Carol on frontend), this should be reformulated as an Optimization problem with a soft-constraint objective.
